1.why: The six screenshots show a static, uncluttered interface with no moving images or pop-ups.

2.why: Large headings, labeled fields, contrasting blue buttons, and highlighted safety notices make important items stand out.

3.why: Each screen presents the main required action prominently, although the logs and repeated safety panel add some distraction.

4.why: The user must complete and track several stages involving a recovery token, verification code, password rules, and privacy acceptance.

5.why: No password-manager support, autofill option, or remember-me control is visible in any screenshot.

6.why: No saved accounts, familiar identifiers, or recognizable saved items are displayed.

7.why: Most instructions are brief and readable, though the technical logs and security wording add complexity.

8.why: No error state or corrective error message is shown in the screenshots.

9.why: The interface states password requirements but provides no concrete example of a valid password, token, or code format near the inputs.

10.why: The required token, code, and password actions are clearly labeled, but no alternative login methods such as face login are offered.

11.why: Each screen presents only one primary task and very few choices at a time.

12.why: The completion screen explicitly confirms that the password was updated, privacy conditions were accepted, and appointment processing can continue.

13.why: Each new step includes a short instruction or tip explaining what the user should enter or do.

14.why: A return-to-start button appears only after completion, and no retry controls or recovery guidance after mistakes are shown.

15.why: All screens consistently use the same layout, typography, colors, panels, labels, and button styling.
